summary: Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. A founder of Waseda University, he served there as a lecturer (1908, 1910) and as Dean of the Faculty of Letters in 1930.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Shin Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami, Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, and under Heinz Bechert, later teaching at Bukkyo University (attested 1999, 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor at Shitennoji University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996, 1999–2016).

Takanori Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and later served as a specially appointed lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied at Waseda University from circa 1968 to 1977. He held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (circa 1996–2010) and Kokugakuin University (circa 2010).

Takanori Unno specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Nagoya University, where he also served as an assistant, and later held teaching posts at Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music and Meijo University.

Takao Hayashi is an Indologist and historian who studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University under David Pingree. He held research and lecturing posts before serving as assistant professor (1986–1989) and professor (1995–2015) at Doshisha University.
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He served as associate professor and professor at Rissho University (~1967–1986), professor at Mejiro University (~1986–2000), and professor at Shinshu University.

Takao Moriyasu was a scholar of Central Asian history who studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He served as associate professor at Kanazawa University and Osaka University, and as professor at Osaka University from 1994 to 2012.

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (circa 1952–1960). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (circa 1969–2003) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions.

Takashi Iwata is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg, and served as associate professor (~1985–1990) and professor (~1990–2014) at Waseda University.
Takashi Koezuka is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Professor (attested 2001) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2012) at Osaka University.
Takashi Maeda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

Takashi Nakao was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He was an associate professor at Bunkyo University Women's College and later professor emeritus at Rissho University.

Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He became an associate professor at Komazawa University in 1991.
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He worked as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute at Taisho University (attested 1978).
